title: Adaptive prefill acceptor safeguard policy and rollback runbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Introduce an adaptive 'prefill acceptor' safeguard layer that evaluates early-prefill probe outputs and decides whether to commit to a fast-path decoder or fall back to a conservative decode. The goal is to reduce tail latency while preventing correctness regressions from overly-optimistic speculative handoffs.
background: We've observed cases where speculative handoffs (fast-path decoders) reduce latency for many requests but occasionally generate low-quality prefixes that downstream decoding can't recover from. Root causes include kernel mismatches, attention truncation heuristics, and miscalibrated acceptance scoring. Current routing heuristics are high-level (score thresholds) and lack a safety layer for corner cases like long-context prompts and models with brittle attention patterns.
proposal: Add a runtime safeguard component that: 1) runs a lightweight prefill probe on candidate handlers with tuned kernel-fit checks and attention-integrity heuristics, 2) computes a multi-dimensional acceptance score (acceptance-confidence) combining early-logit alignment, kernel-affinity score, and latency headroom, 3) applies hysteresis and context-aware thresholds to decide commit vs. fallback, and 4) emits an explicit rollback token that triggers soft-fallback actions when downstream decode shows divergence. The policy will be parameterized so we can A/B different acceptance metric weights and hysteresis windows.
acceptance_metrics: We will surface and use these metrics in the acceptor: 1) early_alignment_score (cosine similarity of probe logits to baseline model logits), 2) kernel_fit_score (historical latency/stability signature match for the kernel & model pair), 3) attention_integrity_index (measures of attention head saturation and unexpected OOM-precursor patterns), 4) accept_latency_margin (percentile headroom relative to SLO), 5) probe_cost_ratio (probe tokens cost vs estimated saved tokens). Acceptance-confidence is a weighted combination and normalized to [0,1]. Thresholds will be context-sensitive (prompt length bucketed by >1024, 256-1024, <256).
fallback_policy: When acceptance-confidence < threshold OR downstream decode drift exceeds threshold, perform: 1) soft-fallback: immediately route remaining decode tokens to conservative model variant with warmed KV cache and kernel-verified path, 2) compensation heuristics: attempt to stitch outputs to minimize discontinuity (prefer complete sentence boundaries), 3) rollback telemetry: mark original request instance with rollback_reason and rollback_latency, and 4) auto-throttle speculative routing for the originating model/kernel pair using exponential backoff counts.
kernel_selection_integration: The acceptor will query the kernel catalog to compute kernel_fit_score based on recent percentiles for token latency, kernel-specific numerical error rates, and quantization mode. If the best kernel for the probe differs in expected behavior from the decode worker's kernel, the acceptor lowers acceptance-confidence. This avoids routing a probe that was run on a high-precision kernel to a low-precision decode path without additional calibration.
attention_optimizations: Attention checks include: peak_attention_norm checks (detects head blowups), prefix_attention_coherence (measures KL between full-context attention distribution and truncated prefix attention), and KV-sparsity heuristics (detects when long-context usage will blow memory). If attention_integrity_index flags high-risk signals, acceptance thresholds are increased and probe scheduling is deferred to favor safe decoding.
prefill_decode_scheduling: Prefill probes run as microbatches scheduled with kernel affinity: prefer to probe on a worker whose kernel fingerprint matches the planned decode worker. Probes are staggered slightly (0-10ms jitter) to spread burst pressure. For high concurrency, we opportunistically reuse recently computed prefix KV caches when probe and decode model are compatible to reduce probe cost.
rollout_plan: 1) Lab validation: controlled benchmark (10k synthetic+real prompts), compare baseline vs acceptor on latency P50/P95/P99, quality regressions (ROUGE/LLR and human blind eval), and rollback rates. 2) Canary: 1% traffic on non-critical orgs for 48h, collect telemetry. 3) Ramp: 10% for 72h, 50% for 72h, then 100% if no regressions. 4) Emergency kill switch: feature flag to disable acceptor and revert to existing routing. Keep runtime-2.6 release gating.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards and alerts: 1) acceptor_accept_rate (by model/kernel/context_bucket), 2) early_alignment_median & p99, 3) rollback_rate and rollback_latency, 4) quality_regression_alert if blind-eval delta > configured threshold, 5) spike alerts if acceptor increases tail latency. All alerts map to SRE runbooks and include a diagnostic trace id to replay probe+decode events.
test_plan: Unit tests for acceptance-score calculation, kernel-fit heuristics, and attention detectors. Integration tests: simulated worker pool with diverse kernel fingerprints to assert correct fallback behavior. Performance test: load generator reproducing typical customer concurrency to verify probe overhead < 3% of token cost and latency SLO preservation. Chaos test: kill fast-path decode worker mid-output and assert soft-fallback completes with no user-facing timeouts.

decisions: Use multi-dimensional acceptance confidence instead of single-threshold heuristics.
Probe should prefer kernel-affine workers to avoid cross-kernel artifact mismatches.
Expose acceptance thresholds as runtime-tunable flags for gradual experimentation.
